$$
v=⟨{t}^{2},\,{e}^{2t}⟩.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector $a.$

activity_context.topic_title: Calculating Acceleration for Plane Motion Using Differentiation

feedback.problem:
The velocity vector $v=⟨u,v⟩$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
v=⟨\frac{3}{t},{5}^{5t}⟩.
$$

Calculate the acceleration vector $a.$
feedback.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{3}{t}),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({5}^{5t})⟩ \\  & =⟨3(-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}),{5}^{5t}\cdot 5\operatorname{ln}⁡5⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{3}{{t}^{2}},{5}^{5t+1}\operatorname{ln}⁡5⟩\end{aligned}
$$
